comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
PREMISE CORRECTION (root-cause investigation, AC1).

The reported behaviour is NOT inconsistent — advisory finding text is published NOWHERE, on EVERY change. Change 1636 is not a counter-example.

Live Gerrit API evidence (RebarBotNava, /a/changes/<n>/...):
- GET revisions/current/comments -> {} (empty) for 1636, 1666 AND 1685. No inline comments on any of them, including the supposed counter-example.
- GET revisions/current/robotcomments -> plain-text body 'robot comments unsupported' for all three. This Gerrit server has robot comments DISABLED/REMOVED, so the bot's robot-comment payload is a dead surface here.
- The rebar-review-bot change message on all three is identical in shape, e.g. 1636 'Patch Set 1: LLM-Review+1 / [LLM-Review: PASS] / rebar code review passed. 2 advisory finding(s) (non-blocking).' — 1666 PS1 says '4 advisory finding(s)', 1685 PS1 says '2 advisory finding(s)'. Count only, in all three cases.

So the earlier '1636 got inline comments' observation was mistaken (most likely rebar review-code local CLI output was read as Gerrit state).

ROOT CAUSE (single, deterministic — not an anchoring or auth failure):
src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py:132 _summarize(), PASS branch, lines 134-138 renders only len(verdict['advisory']) as a count and never itemises the findings. The 'finding' branch (lines 139-152) itemises BLOCKING findings only — advisory text is dropped there too. _translate_findings (adapter.py:114) additionally discards each finding's 'location' field, so no anchor ever reaches the Gerrit layer. voter.py:700 calls gc.post_vote(change_id, revision, value, message) with four positional args, so gerrit_client.post_vote's robot_comments parameter (gerrit_client.py:277-294) is never supplied by production code and always falls back to the single /PATCHSET_LEVEL robot comment carrying the same message string. No code path anywhere constructs a per-file/per-line comment map.

Therefore: hypothesis 'anchor-less findings silently dropped' = partially right (locations ARE discarded, at adapter.py:114) but the mechanism is broader — advisory findings are never rendered at all, anchored or not. Hypotheses 'posting call fails/auth' and 'size threshold' are REJECTED: the vote POST succeeds (LLM-Review+1 landed on all three) and the count is unbounded.

Secondary finding worth carrying into the fix: because robot comments are unsupported on this server, the review message body is the ONLY surface proven to render, so the fix must guarantee body enumeration and treat inline comments as an additive bonus.

comments.body:
Fix implemented in worktree urson-advisory-visibility (branch off origin/main).

New module src/rebar/review_bot/finding_publish.py (211 LOC) owns the publishing surface:
- render_findings_block(findings, kind=...) — EXTRACTED from adapter._summarize's inlined blocking enumeration, so header/truncation/overflow-note wording is defined once and both branches share it. MAX_DETAIL_CHARS=240 / MAX_ITEMS=10 promoted to named constants (the exact pre-fix limits); a test pins byte-identical output for kind='blocking'.
- parse_anchor(location) — same rule as the pre-existing authority rebar.llm.code_review.shim._parse_location, with a reconciliation test asserting the two agree across a table of inputs so they cannot drift. Not shared outright because finding_publish must stay importable without the heavy [agents] extra.
- partition_findings / build_inline_comments — anchorable only when the parsed path is a REAL key of the revision file map AND a line number is present; inline comments carry unresolved=false so an advisory can never hold up submission.
- post_review(...) — casts the vote with comments attached; on GerritError retries message-only with a notice naming the durable code_review artifact. A 409 (change closed) is re-raised untouched so the voter's existing skip path is unchanged, as is a failure of a POST that carried no comments.

adapter.py: _translate_findings now carries 'location' through (additive key); _summarize's PASS branch emits the finding TEXT rather than a bare count, and the 'finding' branch appends advisories too.
gerrit_client.py: new get_revision_files (get_merge_files delegates to it, so the endpoint call exists once); post_vote gained an optional comments map, included only when non-empty.
voter.py: the line-700 call site now goes through post_review; 791 LOC, under the 800 cap.
docs/adr/0009-review-bot-pipe.md section 3 amended — it documented the outbound vote shape this change extends.

RED-verified: tests/unit/test_review_bot_finding_publish.py (19 tests) failed on the missing module, then the adapter assertions failed against the count-only behaviour, before going green.

Note on the plan-review advisory that predicted this: updating the duck-typed post_vote test doubles was indeed needed — four fakes across tests/unit/test_review_bot.py and tests/unit/test_review_bot_token_metrics.py. That advisory was VISIBLE to me only because the review-plan CLI prints advisories to stdout; had it come through the Gerrit surface this bug is about, I would never have seen it. That is live corroboration of the operator's report.

make lint and make typecheck both pass.

compiled_state.description:
## Context

Operator-declared serious bug: the review-bot's LLM-Review vote publishes only a COUNT of
advisory findings ("PASS. N advisory finding(s) (non-blocking)"), and the finding TEXT is
retrievable nowhere on the Gerrit change. Operator impact, verbatim: "if they're invisible it
makes it difficult for us to determine which advisory findings should be promoted to blocking."
This feeds the pending blocking-lane re-enable work.

## Root cause (AC1 — CONFIRMED, see ticket comment #1 for full evidence)

Premise correction: the behaviour is NOT inconsistent. Advisory text is published on NO change.
Change 1636 is not a counter-example — live Gerrit shows `revisions/current/comments` = `{}` and
`robotcomments` = "robot comments unsupported" for 1636, 1666 AND 1685 alike, and all three
carry the same count-only bot message.

Mechanism, single and deterministic:
1. `src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py:132` `_summarize()`, PASS branch (lines 134-138) renders only
   `len(verdict["advisory"])`. It never itemises the findings.
2. The `"finding"` branch (lines 139-152) itemises BLOCKING findings only — advisory text is
   dropped there too, so a BLOCK vote hides advisories as well.
3. `_translate_findings` (`adapter.py:114`) copies `{severity, dimension, detail}` and DISCARDS
   each finding's `location`, so no file/line anchor ever reaches the Gerrit layer.
4. `voter.py:700` calls `gc.post_vote(change_id, revision, value, message)` — four positional
   args — so `post_vote`'s `robot_comments` parameter (`gerrit_client.py:277-294`) is never
   supplied in production and always falls back to one `/PATCHSET_LEVEL` robot comment carrying
   the same message string. No code path builds a per-file comment map.

Rejected hypotheses: posting failure / auth (the vote POST succeeds — LLM-Review+1 landed on all
three) and a size or count threshold (the count is unbounded).

Environmental constraint the fix must respect: robot comments are DISABLED on this Gerrit server,
so the review message body is the only surface proven to render. Body enumeration is therefore
the guaranteed surface; inline comments are additive.

## Plan

New module `src/rebar/review_bot/finding_publish.py` (keeps `voter.py`, currently 778 LOC, under
the 800 cap). It OWNS the enumeration logic that `adapter.py:141-152` currently inlines for
blocking findings — that block is EXTRACTED here and both adapter branches call it, so the
rendering is defined once, not re-implemented:
- `MAX_DETAIL_CHARS = 240` and `MAX_ITEMS = 10` — the exact limits `adapter.py:145-152` uses
  today, promoted to named constants and imported by `adapter.py`.
- `render_findings_block(findings, kind)` — a header line, then up to `MAX_ITEMS` lines of
  `- (criterion) detail [location]` with `detail` truncated to `MAX_DETAIL_CHARS` (ellipsis
  suffix), then an `"N additional <kind> finding(s) omitted from this summary."` note when
  `len(findings) > MAX_ITEMS`. Byte-identical output to today's blocking block for `kind`
  `"blocking"`.
- `parse_anchor(location)` — split a free-text `location` into `(path, line|None)`, tolerating a
  missing or non-numeric line tail; `None` when there is no usable path.
- `partition_findings(findings, revision_paths)` — anchorable only when the parsed path is a key
  of the revision file map; everything else is anchor-less.
- `build_inline_comments(anchorable)` — `{path: [{line, message, unresolved: false}]}`.
  `unresolved: false` keeps the "no unresolved comments" submit requirement untouched.

`gerrit_client.py`: add `GerritClient.get_revision_files(change_id, revision)` — the plain
`GET /a/changes/<id>/revisions/<rev>/files`, valid for ANY revision. The existing
`get_merge_files` (`gerrit_client.py:184`) delegates to it so the endpoint call exists once and
its merge-specific docstring stays accurate. `post_vote` (`gerrit_client.py:277`) gains an
optional `comments` mapping, included in the review body only when non-empty; the
`robot_comments` default is unchanged (AC5).

`adapter.py`: `_translate_findings` (line 114) also carries `location` through (additive key;
existing consumers of `{severity, dimension, detail}` are unaffected). `_summarize` PASS branch
(lines 134-138) keeps its count sentence and appends `render_findings_block(advisory,
"advisory")`; the `"finding"` branch (lines 139-152) calls `render_findings_block` for blocking
and then appends the advisory block.

`voter.py` (minimal delta at the `post_vote` call site, line 700): call
`gc.get_revision_files(...)` inside a `try/except` — ANY failure degrades to an empty path set,
i.e. zero anchorable findings and body-only publication, never a failed vote. Partition, then
post with `comments=`. On `GerritError` from the comment-bearing POST, retry message-only with an
appended notice (AC3) and only then treat a second failure as today's fail-closed error.

Design tradeoff, stated deliberately: EVERY advisory is enumerated in the message body, and
anchorable ones are ALSO posted inline. Duplication is cheap; invisibility is the bug, and the
body is the only surface this server is proven to render.

## Testing

Run from the worktree venv: `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py tests/unit/test_review_bot_finding_publish.py -q`,
then `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint` and `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck`.
Each AC4 sub-case is a named test in `tests/unit/test_review_bot_finding_publish.py`, RED-verified
by running it against unpatched `main` first.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — Root cause identified and recorded as a ticket comment (checked: comment #1 cites the live `GET /a/changes/<n>/revisions/current/comments` and `/robotcomments` responses), with the operator's
  "1636 is a counter-example" premise corrected against live Gerrit API state.
- [ ] AC2 — Every advisory finding is retrievable from the Gerrit change: enumerated in the
  review message body on both the PASS and the BLOCK path, and additionally posted as an inline
  comment when its location anchors to a real path in the revision.
- [ ] AC3 — A comment-posting failure is never silent: the vote still lands, and its message
  carries an explicit notice naming inline publication as failed and pointing at the durable
  `code_review` artifact (`emit_code_review_artifact` -> `rebar.llm.code_review.sidecar.emit`) as
  the full record. Checked by the AC4(e) test asserting the notice substring in the posted message.
- [ ] AC4 — Regression tests pin: (a) advisory findings appear as text in the PASS message
  (the reproduced 1666/1685 condition — RED against current main, which emits a count only);
  (b) advisory text also appears on the BLOCK path; (c) an anchorable finding produces an inline
  comment keyed by path with `unresolved: false`; (d) an anchor-less or off-revision finding is
  still enumerated in the body and produces no inline comment; (e) a `GerritError` on the
  comment-bearing POST falls back to a message-only vote carrying the failure notice.
- [ ] AC5 — `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint` and `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck` pass; no change to vote semantics — label name,
  vote values, PASS/BLOCK mapping, fail-closed coverage-gap behaviour and the dedup/retry
  bookkeeping are all untouched.
